# snowden-turnkey-tyranny-2013

- **URL:** https://www.mic.com/articles/47355/edward-snowden-interview-transcript-full-text-read-the-guardian-s-entire-interview-with-the-man-who-leaked-prism (transcript of the June 2013 Guardian video interview by Glenn Greenwald/Laura Poitras) · **Accessed:** 2026-08-25 · **For:** v1→v2 response round, exact wording of the "turnkey tyranny" passage
- **What it establishes:** Snowden's own framing of the danger as *latent architecture*: the surveillance apparatus is constrained only by policy, so a future leader need only "find the switch." This is the popular/whistleblower statement of the standing-capability argument (cf. Binney's earlier "turnkey totalitarian state," 2012 — Snowden's phrase echoes Binney's).
- **Key passages:** (verified verbatim against the Mic transcript of the Guardian video interview, June 2013)
  - "The greatest fear that I have regarding the outcome for America of these disclosures is that nothing will change. People will see in the media all of these disclosures. They'll know the lengths that the government is going to grant themselves powers unilaterally to create greater control over American society and global society. But they won't be willing to take the risks necessary to stand up and fight to change things to force their representatives to actually take a stand in their interests."
  - "And the months ahead, the years ahead it's only going to get worse until eventually there will be a time where policies will change because the only thing that restricts the activities of the surveillance state are policy. Even our agreements with other sovereign governments, we consider that to be a stipulation of policy rather then a stipulation of law. And because of that a new leader will be elected, they'll find the switch, say that 'Because of the crisis, because of the dangers we face in the world, some new and unpredicted threat, we need more authority, we need more power.' And there will be nothing the people can do at that point to oppose it. And it will be turnkey tyranny."
  - Transcription caution: this is a transcript of spoken remarks from the Guardian's June 9, 2013 video; the Mic text reads "rather then a stipulation of law" (sic). Other outlets' transcripts render it "rather than" and vary in light punctuation. If print-quoting at length, either quote from this transcript with "[sic]"/silent standardization per house style, or check against the Guardian video itself.
- **Reliability:** Secondary carrier (Mic) of a primary interview (Guardian video, June 9, 2013, Hong Kong); the "turnkey tyranny" phrase is universally attested across transcripts. Wording is spoken-word transcription, hence minor variance between carriers.
- **Relevance to this project:** Bears on any latent-capability / "the apparatus awaits its abuser" argument and on the essay's genealogy of the turnkey metaphor (Binney 2012 → Snowden 2013). Use the two-paragraph block above; "they'll find the switch" and "And it will be turnkey tyranny." are the load-bearing verbatim phrases.
